claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films or nanoribbons have a fine-grained structure and high defect density.
The as-deposited material has a heterogeneous distribution of magnetic exchange energies.
High defect density and small grain size provide domain-wall pinning centers.
Post-deposition annealing will enlarge grains and reduce defect and grain-boundary density in FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons.
Annealing reduces internal lattice strain and chemical inhomogeneity.
Annealing makes the distribution of magnetic exchange interactions more uniform.
Reducing pinning sites facilitates more uniform magnetic-domain reorientation.
Greater grain size and reduced microstructural pinning will lower coercivity and narrow the hysteresis loop.
Annealing-induced microstructural homogenization will increase the isothermal magnetocaloric entropy change.
The baseline defects and nanoscale grain boundaries cause significant hysteresis in the as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi material.
The broad distribution of exchange interactions in the as-deposited material reduces its effective magnetocaloric response.
The proposed effect should be observable at applied fields below 100 mT near the magnetic transition temperature.
Nanoscale heat-transfer rates limit the usable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency and may obscure microstructural effects.
Annealing parameters can affect interfacial or precipitate-related behavior.
The annealing treatment should be selected to avoid oxidation and interdiffusion.
Failure to obtain both a statistically significant coercivity reduction and magnetocaloric entropy-change enhancement relative to an as-deposited control would falsify the proposed mechanism.
